subject: Bench kickoff checklist: probe definitions, streaming TTFB, and reproducibility notes
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@fastretail.com>, ops@fastretail.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Bench kickoff checklist: probe definitions, streaming TTFB, and reproducibility notes

Alex / FastRetail team,

Thanks again for the session earlier  it was helpful to walk through the checkout and recommendation flows. I summarized the technical commitments and a tight set of next steps so we can get a reproducible baseline on staging. If anything below needs to be adjusted, flag it and we'll iterate.

High-level goals:
- Confirm Redwood can meet a p95 model emit latency <= 150 ms for 128-token responses for the checkout confirmations path.
- Validate sustained throughput of 600 qps and safe handling of 1,200 concurrent bursts for short windows (~20s).
- Verify streaming behavior and separate out time-to-first-byte (TTFB) vs full-response latency for client integration.

Deliverables and owners (short bullets):
- FastRetail: seed prompt set + three traffic profiles (steady, burst, long-tail) and 3 session templates for KV priming. Attachment expected: fastretail-prompt-samples.json. (Alex)
- Redwood runtime: completed harness_spec.md with the YAML config we will run on staging plus the reproducibility checklist. Marcus will post the harness config and a sample command line run. (Marcus)
- Engineering sync: define deterministic sampling (rng seed, top-p/top-k, temperature) and how we capture model-side tokens vs network-side metrics. Stephanie will add a short section in harness_spec.md on RNG locking. (Stephanie)

Measurement definitions we propose to lock down now:
- Latency reference point: measure at the server emit event (after queuing + compute, before egress network serialization). Report p50/p95/p99.
- TTFB (streaming): measured from request acceptance to first byte emitted to the stream. Capture median and p95.
- Warm-up rules: run warm-up until either 10k model tokens emitted OR 10 minutes of steady traffic have completed. After warm-up, run each profile for 10 minutes to collect stable metrics.
- Token accounting: count input + output tokens at the model boundary for cost/throughput comparisons.
- KV cache: run two phases  cold (no priming) and primed (use provided session templates) to show delta in latency and throughput.

Proposed schedule:
- Apr 18 EOD PST: FastRetail pushes prompt samples + traffic profiles.
- Apr 19: Redwood posts harness config and reproducibility checklist.
- Apr 20: 60-min kickoff to run baseline on staging and walk through initial graphs.

Attachments: prompt_pack_v2.json (template), harness_spec.md (draft).

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Chen
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com

Attachments: prompt_pack_v2.json, harness_spec.md

From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@fastretail.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastretail.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bench kickoff checklist: probe definitions, streaming TTFB, and reproducibility notes

Ava, Marcus,

Appreciate the concise plan. A couple of clarifications from the engineering team so your harness can mirror our production traffic shape: 

- Streaming expectations: our client wants byte-level streaming with interleaved JSON metadata updates (orderId, status flags). For reproducibility, we care about TTFB and first JSON metadata emit as separate metrics.
- Response size: most responses will fall between 32 and 160 tokens; treating 128 as a median makes sense.
- Traffic shape: steady 600 qps, bursts to 1,200 concurrent requests for ~20s, and a long-tail with ~2% of requests > 1s.
- KV priming: we'll provide 3 session templates with repeated user/cart patterns. Please confirm how staging will maintain KV state across simulated sessions.

Also: we will upload fastretail-prompt-samples.json (220 prompts) with a README describing label schema and expected payload structure. ETA Apr 18 EOD PST.

Question: what RNG seeding do you recommend in the harness to make generation deterministic for apples-to-apples comparisons? Can you include recommended sampling params (top-p, temperature, top-k) and a sample harness flag to lock randomness?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morales
Lead Platform Engineer, FastRetail
alex.morales@fastretail.com

Attachment: fastretail-prompt-samples.json

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@fastretail.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bench kickoff checklist: probe definitions, streaming TTFB, and reproducibility notes

Alex,

Thanks  a few technical notes from the runtime side and confirmation of what we'll include in harness_spec.md: 

1) Deterministic sampling: our harness supports a --rng-seed flag that locks the PRNG used for sampling. For exact repeatability we recommend setting temperature=0 and deterministic sampling (greedy) for latency baselines; for quality checks run a matched pair with seed + temperature>0 and record generation variance. We'll add sample CLI snippets.

2) KV cache: on staging we run a lightweight state store that persists KV entries per session ID for the duration of a run. To reproduce, include session_id in each request header and use the provided session templates. We'll include a small helper script to prime KV prior to the main run.

3) Measurement hooks: the harness will emit both TTFB and full-response emit timestamps, and tag events with the traffic profile and session template. Metrics will be written to Prometheus + a JSON artifact for post-run analysis.

4) Warm-up and run lengths: we'll implement the warm-up rule you agreed on (10k model tokens OR 10 minutes), then run each profile for 10 minutes and store raw traces.

I'll attach the initial harness_spec.md and a tiny reproducibility checklist once it's cleaned up (target Apr 19 morning).

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: harness_spec.md (draft)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bench kickoff checklist: probe definitions, streaming TTFB, and reproducibility notes

Alex,

Thanks  confirm receipt of your prompt pack ETA. When you upload, please include the README and the three traffic profile files (steady.json, burst.json, longtail.json). Marcus' team will populate the harness with the following fields: rng_seed, sampling_params, session_templates, and profile definitions.

If everything arrives on Apr 18 EOD as planned, we'll lock a kickoff for Apr 20 at 09:00 PDT and aim to have a first-pass reproducibility report within 48 hours of the run.

Looking forward,
Ava
